description: Extract shared utilities from the monolithic handler into a shared module, then split the handler into four domain-specific Lambda handlers (recipes, ingredients-on-hand, supermarkets, sort-ingredients), and update the CDK stack to create four separate Lambda functions with their respective API Gateway route integrations.
steps: Create apps/api/src/shared/db.ts - export the DynamoDB client setup (DynamoDBClient, DynamoDBDocumentClient) and TABLE_NAME constant. Exact code to extract: `const client = new DynamoDBClient({}); const docClient = DynamoDBDocumentClient.from(client); const TABLE_NAME = process.env['TABLE_NAME'] ?? '';`

Create apps/api/src/shared/bedrock.ts - export the Bedrock client setup. Exact code: `const BEDROCK_REGION = process.env['BEDROCK_REGION'] ?? process.env['AWS_REGION'] ?? 'eu-central-1'; const bedrockClient = new BedrockRuntimeClient({ region: BEDROCK_REGION });`
Create apps/api/src/shared/response.ts - export the corsHeaders object and the response() helper function exactly as they exist in handler.ts

Create apps/api/src/shared/auth.ts - export a getUserId(event: APIGatewayProxyEvent) function that extracts userId from event.requestContext?.authorizer?.['claims']?.['sub'] and returns string | undefined
Create apps/api/src/shared/index.ts - barrel export from all shared modules

Create apps/api/src/handlers/recipes.ts - export a named `handler` of type APIGatewayProxyHandler. Move the recipe CRUD functions here: listRecipes, getRecipe, createRecipe, updateRecipe, deleteRecipe, validateRecipeInput. Also move importRecipe, importRecipeFromText, stripHtmlToText, buildBedrockPrompt, isPrivateOrReservedHost. The handler function should check OPTIONS for CORS, extract userId, then route based on path/method for: GET /recipes, POST /recipes, POST /recipes/import, POST /recipes/import-text, GET /recipes/{id}, PUT /recipes/{id}, DELETE /recipes/{id}. Import shared utilities from ../shared/

Create apps/api/src/handlers/ingredients-on-hand.ts - export a named `handler` of type APIGatewayProxyHandler. Move: listIngredientsOnHand, createIngredientOnHand, deleteIngredientOnHand. Route: GET /ingredients-on-hand, POST /ingredients-on-hand, DELETE /ingredients-on-hand/{id}. Import shared utilities from ../shared/

Create apps/api/src/handlers/supermarkets.ts - export a named `handler` of type APIGatewayProxyHandler. Move: listSupermarkets, createSupermarket, updateSupermarket, deleteSupermarket. Route: GET /supermarkets, POST /supermarkets, PUT /supermarkets/{id}, DELETE /supermarkets/{id}. Import shared utilities from ../shared/

Create apps/api/src/handlers/sort-ingredients.ts - export a named `handler` of type APIGatewayProxyHandler. Move: sortIngredients, sortIngredientsPrompt, sortIngredientsManual, generateSortPrompts. Route: POST /sort-ingredients, POST /sort-ingredients-prompt, POST /sort-ingredients-manual. Import shared utilities from ../shared/

Update apps/api/src/index.ts - export all four handlers with distinct names: export { handler as recipesHandler } from './handlers/recipes'; export { handler as ingredientsOnHandHandler } from './handlers/ingredients-on-hand'; export { handler as supermarketsHandler } from './handlers/supermarkets'; export { handler as sortIngredientsHandler } from './handlers/sort-ingredients';
Delete apps/api/src/handler.ts - it is fully replaced by the new modules

Update apps/infra/src/stacks/recipe-manager-stack.ts: Replace the single NodejsFunction with four NodejsFunction constructs, each with entry pointing to their respective handler file. Create four LambdaIntegration objects. Update the API Gateway resource methods to use the correct integration for each route group. Grant DynamoDB readWriteData to all four Lambdas. Grant Bedrock InvokeModel only to the recipes Lambda and sort-ingredients Lambda (since only they call Bedrock). Each Lambda gets TABLE_NAME env var. The recipes and sort-ingredients Lambdas also get BEDROCK_REGION env var (or inherit from AWS_REGION).
Update .kiro/steering/architecture.md - update the 'Key Decisions' and 'Serverless API' sections to reflect the multi-Lambda architecture with domain-based routing

Update .kiro/steering/conventions.md - update the 'Lambda (apps/api)' section: change 'Single file: apps/api/src/handler.ts' to describe the new multi-handler structure in apps/api/src/handlers/. Update the Handler Pattern section to describe the per-domain handler approach.
acceptance_criteria: apps/api/src/shared/ directory contains db.ts, bedrock.ts, response.ts, auth.ts, index.ts
apps/api/src/handlers/ directory contains recipes.ts, ingredients-on-hand.ts, supermarkets.ts, sort-ingredients.ts
Each handler file exports a named 'handler' of type APIGatewayProxyHandler
apps/api/src/index.ts exports all four handlers with distinct names
CDK stack defines four separate NodejsFunction constructs with correct entry paths
CDK stack routes each API Gateway resource to the correct Lambda integration
Only recipes and sort-ingredients Lambdas have Bedrock permissions
All four Lambdas have DynamoDB read/write permissions and TABLE_NAME env var
pnpm nx build api passes (TypeScript type checking)
pnpm nx build infra passes (CDK stack compiles)
No behavioral change - all routes, request/response formats, CORS handling, and error handling remain identical
